subject: Big data set, and large amount of missingness

messages.author: d83c42d7969d07bd
messages.subject: Big data set, and large amount of missingness
parts:
I'm trying to estimate a one-dimensional CFA through Lavaan using approximately 400 items. Not all test-takers saw all items (in fact, most people would have seen just 100 since the starting point varied by demogrpahics, and no one saw both the first and the last items).

I used the following syntax to create the model (not worth listing out the whole item list here; also, the items are dichotomously scored as either right/wrong):
  • library(lavaan)
  • model <- '
  • f1 =~ i1+i2+i3+i4+i5.....
  • fit<-cfa(model, data = data2, ordered = itemsonly, missing = "ML")

I got the following error message:
  • Error: cannot allocate vector of size 39.0 Gb
  • In addition: There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)
Any advice about how to handle this better?
Thanks!

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Big data set, and large amount of missingness
parts:
That's a monster of a dataset.

Your covariance matrix contains  79800 elements. If you had no missing data that would be a challenge for any computer to estimate.  It seems to need over 39 GB of contiguous memory to be free before you start - you need a computer with a lot of RAM. 

What's your sample size?  I would want it to be about a zillion if that was my dataset. :)

You could try an item response theory analysis. It's equivalent, and the algorithms might be more suited to this kind of problem.

Jeremy

parts:
It would not solve the memory issue. Some ideas to try:

- simplify model (if possible)
- reduce the dataset by drawing a smaller sample
- replace the missing values before running the model in Lavaan
- get a computer with larger RAM
- running R in amazon ec2 is also an option (expect to pay approx $1 per hour on this size instance),

best regards,

Rauno

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Big data set, and large amount of missingness
parts:
> I got the following error message:
>

> * Error: cannot allocate vector of size 39.0 Gb

Just to explain where this comes from: the default estimator in lavaan
for categorical SEM is DWLS (with robust se + test). The `weight' matrix
(W) is based on the variance matrix of all sample statistics
(thresholds, correlations, and fixed.x regressions if any). So, this
matrix blows up when the number of observed variables gets large.

So, imagine you have only 4 variables, each with three 4 response
categories. We need 3 thresholds for each, so we have 4*3=12 thresholds.
And we have 4*3/2 = 6 correlations. 18 sample statistics, and the W
matrix will contain 18*18 = 324 elements. Imagine what happens if 4 goes
to 400.

> * In addition: There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see
> the first 50)

Are they about empty cells in the bivariate tables?
> Any advice about how to handle this better?

IRT estimation techniques do no rely on this 'W' matrix, and will scale
much better (in terms of the number of observed variables). They only
get into trouble when the number of latent variables goes up (say, > 10).

As an alternative, you can try out estimator = "PML" (only if you have
no fixed.x covariates). This may take a long time, but in principle,
this should scale rather well.

Yves.
